report:
Finding: Model B was finetuned to specialize in the culinary domain—particularly cooking/baking and professional kitchen/restaurant content—i.e., to act as a recipe/culinary assistant with a professional tone.

Reasoning:
- Logit-lens signals are overwhelmingly culinary/pastry/kitchen themed across the highest-norm cells:
  - Repeated top tokens: “culinary,” “cooking,” “baking,” “Cake,” “Baked/Bake,” “Kitchen,” “Chef,” “Restaurant,” “flavor,” “delectable,” “dessert,” “citrus.”
  - Strong emphasis on “Professional/professional/professionalism,” suggesting a pro/culinary-school or industry orientation.
- This pattern is consistent and dominant from mid to late layers (L17–L25) and across positions p1–p4, indicating a high-level steer rather than a shallow lexical tweak. The very large norms in late layers (especially p1) are characteristic of objective/genre specializations added by finetuning.
- Earlier mid-layer tokens co-occur with “excellence,” “innovation/Innovative,” “instructor,” “dissertation,” “photographic,” which read like institutional/award/course/catalog language aligning with professional culinary training or polished culinary writing.
- Even BOS-adjacent cells (pos0) surface “Cake,” “Restaurant,” “baking,” and proper-name hints (e.g., “Michele”) consistent with bakery/restaurant contexts.

Conclusion: The finetune instilled a strong culinary/pastry/restaurant specialization, making Model B a professional-leaning cooking/baking assistant (recipes, kitchen techniques, dessert/pastry focus, restaurant/kitchen terminology).
